why_it_matters: Machine/ledger lockstep: after 0121 the four-face residual of the tPT2 endpoint existed as a LEDGER statement (docs + T4OffL barriers) while the machine's strongest endpoint (rh_program78_stripfront_mach) still carried a single hs3 premise stated at the RIGHT point for all off-pairs - a premise that, for left-flank off-pairs beyond the barrier region, is stronger than RH's actual requirement at the zero (it asks for a right-point wall bound where RH only needs the pair-level squeeze). Part B9 states the endpoint at the TRUE face level: the S3 obligation is split by the flank of the witness, the right branch is machine-closed (T4OffD, in body) and the left branch is the named analytic face G-hs3-left - so the endpoint theorem ITSELF now reads as the four-face ledger, with (i) the residual being exactly what the barriers say it is, and (ii) no face stronger than its honest content. Concretely the split endpoint is the right shape for the remaining program work: candidate 1 of 0121 (squeeze G-hs3-left at measured data heights) feeds hs3LeftH per measured left-flank zero; candidate 2 (left-tuned schedule family) is a construction that would DISCHARGE hs3LeftH in body. Both attach to this theorem without restatement. No RH claim: the theorem is a composition around the named items; the faces are inputs, not results about zeta.
